8:["$","p",null,{"className":"x:not-first:mt-[1.25em] x:leading-7","children":["Only a descriptor that declares the files it reads outside its module graph has its answer kept. It declares them by returning ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"hostInputHashes"}],", with a fingerprint for each file it read, or ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"{}"}]," when it read none. b:["$","p",null,{"className":"x:not-first:mt-[1.25em] x:leading-7","children":["A launch whose plugin binary is already cached still has to prove that its inputs did not change. It keeps what it learned under ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"<root>/identities"}]," and ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"<root>/answers"}],", so the next launch does not read every byte of the plugin’s Go source, the installed ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"ttsc"}]," overlay, the Go toolchain and the JavaScript runtime again, or run ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"go list"}]," to rediscover which Go package each plugin entry is. An answer, such as a Go package selection or a runtime’s measured capabilities, is stored under the identities of everything it depends on. The same records serve every later process that proves a plugin source state the load reported: ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"@ttsc/unplugin"}]," workers, capability hosts such as ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"@ttsc/lint"}]," and ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"@ttsc/graph"}],", and ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"ttscserver"}]," confirm the sources and the Go toolchain from metadata instead of reading them again. c:["$","p",null,{"className":"x:not-first:mt-[1.25em] x:leading-7","children":["A recorded digest is reused only while every file in its population still has the recorded identity, size and timestamps, and each modification time is older than a reference the launch writes on the same drive. An edit changes the metadata, and an edit inside the same clock tick as the recorded one fails the reference check, so in both cases the files are read again. The launch writes its references into the cache itself and into a private ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"ttsc-clock-references"}]," directory of the current user below the system temporary directory, so files on any other drive are always read."]}]

A project whose root is itself a plugin’s Go module therefore needs a root elsewhere, or below its ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"node_modules"}],", which the sources never include."]}]
3a:["$","p",null,{"className":"x:not-first:mt-[1.25em] x:leading-7","children":["Relocating costs you automatic cleanup. In the default project-local cache, ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"ttsc"}]," prunes plugin binaries unused for 30 days and runs LRU pruning from a 2 GiB ceiling toward 1.6 GiB. The same policy covers ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"descriptors"}],", ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"capabilities"}],", ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"identities"}],", ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"answers"}],", and ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"ttsx-orphan"}],", where each reuse records a use. It checks at most daily while idle and again after every cold binary publication. The binary returned by that cold build and entries with active build generations are excluded; if those exclusions keep the root above the ceiling, the marker schedules another pass."]}]
3b:["$","p",null,{"className":"x:not-first:mt-[1.25em] x:leading-7","children":["After a cold source-plugin build attempt, including an ordinary failed build, ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"ttsc"}]," prunes its Go object cache from an 8 GiB ceiling toward 6 GiB when native ownership permits it. The newest target-sized cohort remains protected for the requested hour plus Go’s one-hour access-mtime coalescing tolerance. Active builds and maintenance publish heartbeat records. An unguarded stopped build heartbeat receives a one-hour grace; completed maintenance is retired immediately, and an expired maintenance heartbeat receives one minute. These time limits rely on heartbeat freshness and do not prove that a suspended process has ended. A record dated implausibly far in the future is rebased and receives one ordinary grace period."]}]
3c:["$","p",null,{"className":"x:not-first:mt-[1.25em] x:leading-7","children":"Owned native builds also protect their exact scratch inputs, plugin key and shared Go cache until process-tree closure is confirmed. An unknown outcome retains these paths and refuses same-key reuse, GC and clean regardless of PID absence or age; diagnostics identify the retained paths. Independent plugin keys can still build against the shared Go cache. Caller-selected Go caches receive lifetime guard metadata for these owned tasks without becoming subject to ttsc’s size-based eviction. Normal joined or never-started commands release their guards. Recovery requires the original command owner’s confirmed closure, or independent external closure confirmation before manual reclamation; losing that authority leaves the inputs quarantined. Older ttsc versions do not implement these guards and must not share quarantined roots."}]
3d:["$","p",null,{"className":"x:not-first:mt-[1.25em] x:leading-7","children":["A root named through ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"TTSC_CACHE_DIR"}]," or ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"--cache-dir"}]," is not garbage-collected automatically because its caller owns its lifetime. For a ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"TTSC_CACHE_DIR"}]," root, ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"ttsc clean"}]," removes ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"plugins"}],", ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"descriptors"}],", ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"capabilities"}],", ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"identities"}],", ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"answers"}],", ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"ttsx-orphan"}],", runtime directories whose recorded owners are provably gone, and the nested ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"go-build"}]," when the root’s basename is ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"ttsc"}],". A runtime directory stays when its process is alive, its owner is on another host, or its owner record is absent or unreadable."]}]
3e:["$","p",null,{"className":"x:not-first:mt-[1.25em] x:leading-7","children":[["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"ttsc clean --cache-dir <dir>"}]," selects the named directory as a whole, including runtime output still in use. ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"TTSC_GO_CACHE_DIR"}]," follows the same caller-owned lifetime. A caller-provided ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"GOCACHE"}]," stays protected in both cleanup modes: a deletion target that contains it, lies inside it, or has uncertain physical overlap is preserved."]}]
3f:["$","p",null,{"className":"x:not-first:mt-[1.25em] x:leading-7","children":"An owner record that cannot be read or parsed, or a run with no owner record from an older release, leaves ownership unknown, so default clean keeps that run. If the run index itself cannot be listed, clean fails without removing the runtime directory. A new run’s directory and owner record are published under the same lock that default clean holds while it chooses and removes old runs. The run index is pinned to its physical directory before ownership is inspected, so changing a cache link later cannot redirect removal to another run. A dangling link at the runtime root is removed as a link. Each Node child that inherits the runtime manifest records its own ownership before running user code; a live descendant keeps the run’s output after its launcher exits. A child without that manifest uses its own dependency cache and does not claim the parent run."}]
